Algebra I · Lesson 8.3

Solving Linear Inequalities

Solve this lesson →All lessons

An inequality with a letter in it is true at some values of that letter and false at others. Solving it means finding every value that makes it true. The moves are the ones chapter 4 used to solve equations, run under 8.1's rules, and one of those rules is the reason an inequality is not just an equation with a different symbol.

Problem
Every solution of y−23≥46y−23≥46 sits at or above a single number, and that number is itself a solution. Enter that number.
Show a hint
  • The boundary is the yy that makes y−23y−23 exactly 4646, and it counts as a solution because ≥≥ is true when the two sides are equal.
  • Undo the subtraction. Adding 2323 to both sides is one of 8.1's moves that leaves the direction alone, so it clears the −23−23 off the left.
Show the full solution
Adding 2323 to both sides gives y≥69y≥69​. Adding the same amount to both sides leaves the direction alone. At y=69y=69 the left side is exactly 4646, which counts, and at y=68y=68 it is 4545, which does not.
Problem
The solutions of 6w+19<916w+19<91 are exactly the numbers less than one cutoff value, and the cutoff itself is not a solution. Enter the cutoff value.
Show a hint
  • Two moves, in the same order chapter 4 used on equations. Clear the 1919 first, then the coefficient 66.
  • Subtracting 1919 from both sides leaves 6w<726w<72. Six is positive, so the direction of the inequality stays the same when you divide both sides by it.
Show the full solution
Subtract 1919 from both sides for 6w<726w<72, then divide by the positive 66 for w<12w<12​. At w=12w=12 the left side is exactly 9191, and 91<9191<91 is false, so 1212 is the cutoff and not a solution.
Key idea
Solving an inequality means describing every value that makes it true. The equation 6w+19=916w+19=91 holds at w=12w=12 and at no other value, so the whole answer is one number. The inequality 6w+19<916w+19<91 holds at 1111, at 00, at −800−800, and at every number below 1212, so the solutions cannot be listed. The answer is a description instead, the single simple inequality w<12w<12, which is a boundary and a direction and nothing else. Producing that form is the goal of every problem here, the way w=12w=12 was the goal in chapter 4.
Problem
Enter the largest integer tt that satisfies 4t−9<504t−9<50.
Show a hint
  • Describe all the solutions first, then pick the largest integer inside that description.
  • Adding 99 gives 4t<594t<59, and dividing by 44 leaves a boundary that is not a whole number. Test the whole number just below it.
Show the full solution
Add 99 to both sides for 4t<594t<59, then divide by the positive 44 for t<594t<459​. Since 594=14.75459​=14.75, the largest integer allowed is 1414​. Checking, 4(14)−9=474(14)−9=47 is below 5050 while 4(15)−9=514(15)−9=51 is not. The boundary is not a whole number, so no integer sits exactly on it and ≤≤ in place of << would give the same answer.
Problem
A student solves 11−4x≤4911−4x≤49. After subtracting 1111 from both sides, the student divides by −4−4 and leaves the symbol pointing the same way, which makes the resulting statement about xx wrong. Enter the largest integer that fits the student's wrong statement.
Show a hint
  • Follow the student's work rather than your own. Subtracting 1111 gives −4x≤38−4x≤38, and the student then divides by −4−4 while keeping ≤≤.
  • The student's statement is x≤−192x≤−219​, and −192=−9.5−219​=−9.5. No integer equals −9.5−9.5, so take the largest integer below it, and on the negative side larger means closer to zero.
Show the full solution
Subtracting 1111 gives −4x≤38−4x≤38, and dividing by −4−4 without reversing gives x≤−192x≤−219​, so the student's largest integer is −10−10​. Dividing by a negative reverses the symbol, so the true statement is x≥−192x≥−219​ and the smallest integer that works is −9−9. Testing x=−10x=−10 in the original gives 11+40=5111+40=51, above 4949.
Key idea
Isolate the variable exactly as in chapter 4. Undo the last operation first, clearing the constant by adding or subtracting and then clearing the coefficient by dividing, which is 4.2's order. Adding or subtracting the same amount on both sides never changes the direction, and neither does multiplying or dividing by a positive number. Multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number reverses the direction, which is 8.1's rule and the only difference from solving an equation. Dividing −4x≤38−4x≤38 by −4−4 gives x≥−192x≥−219​, not x≤−192x≤−219​.

A negative coefficient is not forced on you. When the variable is on both sides, a variable term can be removed from either side, and one of those two removals leaves a positive coefficient behind. Removing a variable term is a subtraction, so it never reverses the direction. That choice comes up in each of the next two problems.

Problem
Enter the smallest integer kk that satisfies 9k−14>5k+269k−14>5k+26.
Show a hint
  • Once kk has a value, 5k5k is a number, so subtracting 5k5k from both sides is 4.3's move and the direction holds.
  • That leaves 4k−14>264k−14>26. Add 1414, divide by 44, then take the smallest integer strictly above the boundary.
Show the full solution
Subtract 5k5k from both sides for 4k−14>264k−14>26, add 1414 for 4k>404k>40, then divide by 44 for k>10k>10, so the smallest integer is 1111​. At k=10k=10 both sides equal 7676, and >> does not allow equality.
Problem
In 3m+47≤8m+123m+47≤8m+12 the variable terms can be gathered on either side. Use the choice that leaves a positive coefficient, so no reversal is needed. Enter the smallest value mm can take.
Show a hint
  • Subtracting 3m3m from both sides puts the variable on the right with a positive coefficient. Subtracting 8m8m instead leaves −5m−5m on the left, so a division by a negative comes later.
  • Take the first route. Subtracting 3m3m and then 1212 from both sides gives 35≤5m35≤5m.
Show the full solution
Subtract 3m3m from both sides for 47≤5m+1247≤5m+12, subtract 1212 for 35≤5m35≤5m, and divide by the positive 55 for 7≤m7≤m, so the smallest value is 77​. Gathering on the left instead gives −5m≤−35−5m≤−35, and dividing by −5−5 reverses the symbol to m≥7m≥7. Both routes describe the same solutions, but the second has one more step where the direction can be lost.
Key idea
Gather the variable terms onto one side, and choose that side. Once the letter has a value, a term such as 5m5m is a number, so subtracting it from both sides is 4.3's move and the direction holds. Both choices are legal and both give the same description. Subtract the smaller variable term. In 3m+47≤8m+123m+47≤8m+12 that means subtracting 3m3m, which leaves 5m5m on the right and a final division by 55. Subtracting 8m8m instead leaves −5m−5m on the left and a final division by −5−5, which is one more place to lose the direction.

Isolating comes last. Distribute to clear parentheses the 2.1 way, and combine like terms on each side the 2.4 way. Neither move changes the other side, so no question of direction comes up while a side is being cleaned. Clean both sides first, then gather the variable terms and isolate.

Problem
Enter the largest integer xx that satisfies 7(2x−5)−3x<4(x+8)+67(2x−5)−3x<4(x+8)+6.
Show a hint
  • Simplify each side before gathering anything. Distribute both products, then combine like terms on each side separately.
  • The two sides become 11x−3511x−35 and 4x+384x+38. Subtract 4x4x rather than 11x11x, since taking away the smaller coefficient leaves a positive coefficient on xx.
Show the full solution
Distributing and combining gives 11x−35<4x+3811x−35<4x+38. Subtracting 4x4x gives 7x−35<387x−35<38, adding 3535 gives 7x<737x<73, and dividing by 77 gives x<737x<773​. Since 737773​ sits between 1010 and 1111, the largest integer is 1010​. Distributing multiplies both terms inside the parentheses by 77, so 7(2x−5)7(2x−5) is 14x−3514x−35 and not 14x−514x−5.
Fun fact
Joseph Fourier published a method in 1826 for taking a whole system of linear inequalities and removing one unknown at a time from it, the same elimination idea 5.3 used on systems of equations.
Problem
The inequality 3x4−x6≥2143x​−6x​≥21 is true for every xx from one value upward, and that value itself makes it true. Clear the fractions first, then enter that value.
Show a hint
  • The two denominators are 44 and 66. Multiplying both sides by a number that both of them divide leaves no fraction anywhere.
  • Multiplying by 1212 gives 9x−2x≥2529x−2x≥252, and 1212 is positive, so the direction is unchanged.
Show the full solution
Multiply both sides by 1212, a positive number, so the direction is unchanged, giving 9x−2x≥2529x−2x≥252, then 7x≥2527x≥252 and x≥36x≥36​. Checking the endpoint, 3(36)4−366=27−6=2143(36)​−636​=27−6=21, and 21≥2121≥21 is true, so 3636 itself is a solution.
Key idea
Simplify each side before gathering anything. Distributing and combining like terms rewrite one side as an equal expression, so the other side and the direction are unchanged. Clear fractions by multiplying both sides by a positive common denominator. A common denominator is positive by choice, so that step never reverses the direction. Multiplying 3x4−x6≥2143x​−6x​≥21 by 1212 gives 9x−2x≥2529x−2x≥252, with ≥≥ pointing the same way. Multiplying by a negative number instead would clear the fractions and reverse every symbol, so there is no reason to do it.

Gathering the variable terms can remove every one of them, since the two sides can have the same variable part. What is left is a comparison between two numbers with no letter in it. A comparison like that reads the same at every value, true as it stands or false as it stands, so the original holds everywhere or nowhere.

Problem
The statement −13≤4x+7<39−13≤4x+7<39 is a chain, and it says both −13≤4x+7−13≤4x+7 and 4x+7<394x+7<39 at once. Solve it by doing the same thing to all three parts at each step. Enter the smallest value of xx that makes the whole chain true.
Show a hint
  • The middle part is 4x+74x+7, so the first move is subtracting 77, and that subtraction has to be done to −13−13 and to 3939 as well.
  • Subtracting 77 from all three parts gives −20≤4x<32−20≤4x<32. Dividing all three by 44 is dividing by a positive number, so both directions hold.
Show the full solution
Subtract 77 from all three parts for −20≤4x<32−20≤4x<32, then divide all three by the positive 44 for −5≤x<8−5≤x<8, so the smallest value is −5−5​. Checking, 4(−5)+7=−134(−5)+7=−13, and −13≤−13<39−13≤−13<39 is true. Any xx below −5−5 makes 4x+74x+7 less than −13−13, so the left comparison fails.
Problem
Enter how many of the values x=−31x=−31, x=−56x=−65​, x=0x=0, x=4.5x=4.5, x=57x=57 and x=210x=210 satisfy 5(x+9)−2x>3x+385(x+9)−2x>3x+38.
Show a hint
  • Testing each value one at a time is the long route. Simplify the left side and gather the variable terms first, then see what is left.
  • The left side collects to 3x+453x+45, so both sides carry 3x3x. Subtracting 3x3x removes the letter entirely.
Show the full solution
Distributing gives 5x+45−2x=3x+455x+45−2x=3x+45 on the left, so the inequality is 3x+45>3x+383x+45>3x+38. Subtracting 3x3x from both sides leaves 45>3845>38, which is true and contains no xx, so every real number is a solution and the count is 66​. A true numerical statement at the end means the inequality holds everywhere, whatever the listed values happened to be.
Key idea
When every variable term cancels, the numerical statement left behind is the whole answer. If it is true, such as 45>3845>38, the original holds at every real number and every value is a solution. If it is false, such as −6>9−6>9, the original holds nowhere and there are no solutions. These are 4.3's two endings for equations, the identity and the no-solutions case, reached the same way and read the same way. Watch for the lookalike. If a variable term remains, nothing special has happened and the inequality is an ordinary one.

Check a finished description with two substitutions. Put the boundary value into the original and see whether it holds, which settles whether the boundary itself counts. Then test one value from the described side. A missed reversal shows up on that second test, since with the direction backwards every value in the description fails the original.

Problem
Enter how many integers xx with −15≤x≤15−15≤x≤15 satisfy 9−2x>3x−319−2x>3x−31. The inequality on its own has infinitely many integer solutions, so only the ones inside the stated range are counted.
Show a hint
  • Both sides have an xx term, so gather them on one side before anything else. Collect them where the coefficient comes out positive and no step will divide by a negative.
  • Adding 2x2x and then 3131 to both sides gives 40>5x40>5x. That sets only the top of the allowed range, since the bottom is the stated −15−15. The symbol is strict, so check whether the cutoff value itself counts.
Show the full solution
Adding 2x2x and 3131 to both sides gives 40>5x40>5x, so x<8x<8. Inside −15≤x≤15−15≤x≤15 the allowed integers run from −15−15 to 77, and 7−(−15)+1=237−(−15)+1=23​. Checking, x=7x=7 gives −5>−10−5>−10, true, and x=8x=8 gives −7>−7−7>−7, false. Adding 2x2x rather than subtracting 3x3x keeps the coefficient positive and removes the reversal step.
Problem
Enter how many integers xx satisfy −7<13−3x2≤5−7<213−3x​≤5. Both ends of the solved form are integers, so test each one in the original inequality before counting.
Show a hint
  • Clear the fraction first by multiplying all three parts by 22. That multiplier is positive, so neither direction reverses.
  • Subtracting 1313 from all three parts leaves −27<−3x≤−3−27<−3x≤−3. Dividing all three by −3−3 reverses both directions, so the ≤≤ end becomes the lower end.
Show the full solution
Multiplying all three parts by 22 gives −14<13−3x≤10−14<13−3x≤10, subtracting 1313 gives −27<−3x≤−3−27<−3x≤−3, and dividing all three by −3−3 reverses both directions to 9>x≥19>x≥1, which reads 1≤x<91≤x<9. The integers are 11 through 88, so the count is 88​. Test both ends in the original. At x=1x=1 the middle part is 55, and 5≤55≤5 is true, so 11 is in. At x=9x=9 the middle part is −7−7, and −7<−7−7<−7 is false, so 99 is out.

Every answer here was described in words and symbols, a boundary together with the direction that goes with it. Lesson 8.4, Graphing Inequalities, is where those descriptions are drawn instead. On a number line the boundary is one marked point and the solutions are everything on one side of it, and with two letters the picture is a region of the plane.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A number xx satisfies x+38≤55x+38≤55. Enter the largest value xx can be.
Show the solution
Subtracting 3838 from both sides leaves the direction unchanged, giving x≤17x≤17​. Since ≤≤ means less than or equal to, x=17x=17 is allowed, and checking, 17+38=5517+38=55.
Practice
Enter the smallest integer pp that satisfies p5+7>165p​+7>16.
Show the solution
Subtracting 77 gives p5>95p​>9, and multiplying both sides by the positive 55 gives p>45p>45, so the smallest integer is 4646​. At p=45p=45 the left side equals 1616 exactly, which is not greater than 1616.
Practice
Enter the smallest integer xx that satisfies −3x<24−3x<24.
Show the solution
Dividing both sides by −3−3 reverses the direction to x>−8x>−8, so the smallest integer is −7−7​. Checking, −3(−7)=21<24−3(−7)=21<24 while −3(−8)=24−3(−8)=24 is not below 2424.
Practice
Solve 5k−24≥715k−24≥71. The solutions are exactly the values of kk at or above a single number, and that number is itself a solution. Enter that number.
Show the solution
Adding 2424 to both sides gives 5k≥955k≥95, and dividing both sides by 55 leaves the direction alone, so k≥19k≥19​. At k=19k=19 the left side is exactly 7171, and ≥≥ includes that boundary.
Practice
Enter the largest integer yy that satisfies 8y+11<1228y+11<122.
Show the solution
Subtracting 1111 gives 8y<1118y<111, and dividing by 88 gives y<1118=13.875y<8111​=13.875, so the largest integer is 1313​. Checking, 8(13)+11=115<1228(13)+11=115<122 while 8(14)+11=1238(14)+11=123 is not below 122122.
Practice
A number xx satisfies 20−4x≥5220−4x≥52. Enter the largest value xx can be.
Show the solution
Subtracting 2020 gives −4x≥32−4x≥32, and dividing by −4−4 reverses the direction to x≤−8x≤−8​. At x=−8x=−8 the left side is 20−4(−8)=5220−4(−8)=52, which is allowed since the comparison is ≥≥, while x=−7x=−7 gives 4848. Skipping the reversal would give x≥−8x≥−8, which is false at x=0x=0, where the left side is 2020.
Practice
Enter the smallest integer vv that satisfies 12v−5>5v+10012v−5>5v+100.
Show the solution
Subtracting 5v5v gives 7v−5>1007v−5>100, adding 55 gives 7v>1057v>105, and dividing by 77 gives v>15v>15, so the smallest integer is 1616​. At v=15v=15 both sides equal 175175, and the bound is strict, so 1515 is ruled out.
Practice
Enter how many integers nn with −10≤n≤30−10≤n≤30 satisfy 4n−9<3n+134n−9<3n+13.
Show the solution
Subtracting 3n3n gives n−9<13n−9<13, so n<22n<22. Inside −10≤n≤30−10≤n≤30 the integers allowed run from −10−10 to 2121, and 21−(−10)+1=3221−(−10)+1=32​. Subtracting the two endpoints without adding 11 gives 3131 and misses one of the two ends.
Practice
Enter the largest value of xx that satisfies 6x+5≤4x+126x+5≤4x+12, as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Subtracting 4x4x gives 2x+5≤122x+5≤12, subtracting 55 gives 2x≤72x≤7, and dividing by the positive number 22 keeps the direction, giving x≤72x≤27​​. Both sides equal 2626 at x=72x=27​, and since the comparison is ≤≤ rather than <<, that boundary value is itself a solution.
Practice
The inequality 3(2x+7)−5x≥2(x−4)+93(2x+7)−5x≥2(x−4)+9 holds for every xx at or below one value, and that value satisfies it too. Enter that value.
Show the solution
Distributing and combining gives x+21≥2x+1x+21≥2x+1. Subtracting xx from both sides gives 21≥x+121≥x+1, and subtracting 11 gives 20≥x20≥x, so x≤20x≤20​. At x=20x=20 both sides equal 4141, and a ≥≥ statement is true when the two sides are equal, so 2020 itself is a solution.
Practice
Solve x3+x4>143x​+4x​>14. Enter the largest number that is not a solution.
Show the solution
Multiplying both sides by the positive number 1212 keeps the direction, giving 4x+3x>1684x+3x>168, so 7x>1687x>168 and x>24x>24​. Every number above 2424 is a solution and 2424 is not, since at x=24x=24 the left side is 8+6=148+6=14, which is not greater than 1414.
Practice
Enter the smallest integer xx that satisfies −11<5x+4≤34−11<5x+4≤34.
Show the solution
Subtracting 44 from all three parts gives −15<5x≤30−15<5x≤30, and dividing all three by the positive 55 gives −3<x≤6−3<x≤6, so the smallest integer is −2−2​. The left end is strict, so −3−3 is excluded even though 5(−3)+4=−115(−3)+4=−11 sits right at it.
Practice
Enter the largest integer xx that satisfies 1≤8−3x<201≤8−3x<20.
Show the solution
Subtracting 88 from all three parts gives −7≤−3x<12−7≤−3x<12, and dividing all three by −3−3 reverses both symbols to 73≥x>−437​≥x>−4, which reads −4<x≤73−4<x≤37​. The largest integer is 22​. Checking, 8−3(2)=28−3(2)=2 satisfies the chain while 8−3(3)=−18−3(3)=−1 falls below 11.
Practice
Test the five values x=−30x=−30, x=−12x=−21​, x=6.5x=6.5, x=41x=41 and x=88x=88 in 7(x−2)−3x≥4x+57(x−2)−3x≥4x+5. Enter how many of them satisfy the inequality.
Show the solution
Distributing gives 7x−14−3x=4x−147x−14−3x=4x−14, so the inequality reads 4x−14≥4x+54x−14≥4x+5. Subtracting 4x4x from both sides leaves −14≥5−14≥5, which is false, so no value of xx works and the count is 00​. Once the variable cancels and a false number statement is left, the inequality has no solutions no matter which values are tested.
Practice
A student solves 3(8−2x)>x−413(8−2x)>x−41. After distributing and gathering the variable terms on the left, the student divides by the negative coefficient and keeps the symbol pointing the same way. Enter the largest integer that actually satisfies the original inequality.
Show the solution
Distributing gives 24−6x>x−4124−6x>x−41, subtracting xx and 2424 from both sides gives −7x>−65−7x>−65, and dividing by −7−7 reverses the direction to x<657x<765​, so the largest integer is 99​. Checking, x=9x=9 gives −30>−32−30>−32 while x=10x=10 gives −36>−31−36>−31, which is false. Without the reversal the description comes out as x>657x>765​, the same boundary pointing the wrong way.
Practice
Enter the largest integer xx that satisfies 2x−13−x+25<x15+132x−1​−5x+2​<15x​+1.
Show the solution
Multiplying by the positive 1515 gives 5(2x−1)−3(x+2)<x+155(2x−1)−3(x+2)<x+15, which is 7x−11<x+157x−11<x+15. Subtracting xx and adding 1111 gives 6x<266x<26, so x<133x<313​ and the largest integer is 44​. Distributing −3−3 over x+2x+2 gives −3x−6−3x−6. Writing +6+6 there instead changes the boundary and the answer with it.
Practice
Enter how many integers xx satisfy −6≤5−2x4<3−6≤45−2x​<3.
Show the solution
Multiplying all three parts by 44 gives −24≤5−2x<12−24≤5−2x<12, subtracting 55 gives −29≤−2x<7−29≤−2x<7, and dividing all three parts by −2−2 reverses both directions to 292≥x>−72229​≥x>−27​, which reads −72<x≤292−27​<x≤229​. The integers run from −3−3 to 1414, so the count is 14−(−3)+1=1814−(−3)+1=18​. Both boundaries are fractions here, so no integer sits exactly on either end.
